title: Air India Group Adds One Aircraft Per Week as 600-Plane Fleet Overhaul Accelerates
excerpt: The Tata-owned carrier has 524 jets still to come by 2031, with new wide-body deliveries every six weeks and most suspended international routes set to resume in September.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Air India is adding one aircraft weekly, with 524 jets still to be delivered by 2031.
  • The airline expects new wide-body aircraft deliveries every six weeks for 18 months.
  • So far, Air India has received 57 jets from its historic 600-aircraft order.
  • Temporary capacity cuts on US and European routes are expected to end by September 2026.

Currently Operated Aircraft
  • Air India Group is adding aircraft at a rate of one per week, with over 50 new planes scheduled for delivery in 2026 as part of its 600-aircraft order from Airbus and Boeing
  • The airline expects to receive one new wide-body aircraft every six weeks for the next 18 months, including Airbus A350-1000s and Boeing 787-9s
  • Air India has received 57 jets so far from its original order, with 524 aircraft still pending delivery through 2031
  • The fleet expansion comes amid temporary capacity cuts on US and European routes, with full service restoration expected from September 2026

Air India Group is in the midst of one of the largest fleet expansions in global aviation history. The Tata Group-owned carrier is now receiving new aircraft at a rate of roughly one per week, matching the delivery pace of larger rival IndiGo and signaling a decisive phase in its multi-billion-dollar transformation from a struggling state-owned airline into a competitive global carrier.

"We have 524 aircraft yet to be delivered. And all of those will come by around 2031. We will be taking an aircraft about once every six days, including Air India Express, for the next few years," Air India CEO Campbell Wilson said at an industry event in New Delhi, according to Livemint.

The Scale of the Order

Air India's fleet overhaul began in June 2023 with a landmark order for 470 aircraft from Airbus and Boeing — at the time, the largest single airline order in commercial aviation history. The airline subsequently added 100 more Airbus jets and, in January 2026 at the Wings India air show in Hyderabad, ordered an additional 30 Boeing 737 MAX aircraft and converted part of its existing Airbus order to 15 long-range A321XLR jets, according to Reuters.

The total order book now stands at 600 aircraft. Air India has received 57 jets so far, including 51 Boeing 737 MAX planes and six Airbus A350s, according to The Hindu Business Line. The airline currently operates 187 aircraft — 127 narrow-body and 60 wide-body jets — with Air India Express adding another 110 to bring the combined group fleet to roughly 297 planes.

Wide-Body Deliveries in Focus

For long-haul operations, Air India is set to induct six new wide-body aircraft in 2026, receiving one every six weeks for the next 18 months. These will include the Airbus A350-1000, the airline's first of the type, and additional Boeing 787-9 Dreamliners built with bespoke cabin interiors installed directly on the production line.

The first custom-built 787-9, registered VT-AWA, was ferried non-stop from Boeing's Everett facility to New Delhi earlier this year. By the end of 2026, nearly 60% of Air India's wide-body fleet is expected to feature modernized cabin interiors, according to the airline.

"This additional order for 30 Boeing 737 aircraft is part of our broader fleet strategy to position Air India firmly for the future, as a world-class global carrier that India deserves and the world expects."

— Campbell Wilson, CEO, Air India

Capacity Challenges and Route Restoration

The expansion comes during a difficult operational period. Air India temporarily reduced domestic capacity by 10% to 15% between June and August and suspended several international routes, including services to Chicago O'Hare and Washington Dulles. The airline attributed the cuts to a combination of fleet retrofit programs, delivery delays from manufacturers, and the retirement of older Boeing 777-200LR aircraft.

Nipun Aggarwal, Air India's Chief Commercial and Transformation Officer, said at a FAITH tourism conference in New Delhi that most suspended services will be restored from September, with European operations progressively resuming through August, according to Aviation A2Z. Chicago and Washington routes, however, will remain unavailable due to continued aircraft shortages.

Wilson also cited geopolitical headwinds — the closure of Pakistani airspace, Middle East tensions, 50% US tariffs on Indian goods, and constraints on H-1B visas — as "unprecedented shocks to the system."

What This Means for Indian Diaspora Travelers

For the millions of Indians living abroad, Air India's fleet transformation directly affects the quality and availability of nonstop flights between India and major diaspora hubs. The A350-1000s and new 787-9s will bring substantially upgraded cabins on long-haul routes to North America, Europe, and the Gulf. Newark is among the destinations set to regain additional frequencies from September, though travelers to Chicago and Washington will need to wait longer.

The competitive picture is also shifting. IndiGo, which holds 64.2% of India's domestic market versus Air India Group's 27.3%, expects 100 Airbus deliveries through 2027. But analysts note that roughly 33% of Air India's supply comes from Boeing, whose delivery track record has been less reliable than Airbus's in recent years.

"If Air India is adding one aircraft a week, then yes, they would be matching IndiGo on the pace of supply additions," said Shobit Singhal, associate director at Anand Rathi Institutional Equities. "But uncertainty over deliveries hangs over the order on Boeing."

Air India's Fleet Expansion Timeline
June 2023
Fleet overhaul begins with a landmark order for 470 aircraft.
2026
Air India to receive one new wide-body aircraft every six weeks.
September 2026
Full service restoration expected on suspended international routes.
